metadata.description: Curated primary sources for API contract testing, compatibility gates, schema validation, and mixed-protocol contract workflows.
metadata.title: QA Api Testing Contracts - Sources

specifications.name: OpenAPI Specification v3.2.0
specifications.relevance: Current published OpenAPI line for HTTP API contracts. Use OpenAPI 3.1 in examples when tool support for 3.2 is unclear.

specifications.name: OAI sig-moonwalk (OpenAPI 4.0 / "Project Moonwalk")
specifications.relevance: OpenAPI 4.0 design effort. Confirmed as of 2026-07-11: still in design/ADR phase, no stable specification, no production tooling support, no committed release date. The SIG's own guidance is to keep using OpenAPI 3.x today. Do not plan contract-testing pipelines around 4.0 features.

specifications.name: JSON Schema (2020-12)
specifications.relevance: Core validation model used by OpenAPI 3.1+ and related tooling.

specifications.name: AsyncAPI Specification v3.1.0
specifications.relevance: Canonical contract surface for event-driven APIs, messages, and channels. v3.1.0 is the current stable release (January 2026); minor release over v3.0.0 with no breaking changes.

specifications.name: Arazzo Specification v1.1.0
specifications.relevance: Workflow contract format for multi-step API outcomes and dependent call sequences. v1.1.0 released May 18, 2026 (minor release over 1.0.1, Jan 2025), backward-compatible; adds AsyncAPI-referencing steps, JSONPath/XPath support, and $self identity referencing.

specifications.name: OpenAPI Initiative – Arazzo Specification Overview
specifications.relevance: OAI landing page for Arazzo: purpose, current version (1.1.0 as of May 2026), and conformance test suite. AsyncAPI workflow support shipped in 1.1.0 (previously roadmap).

specifications.name: GraphQL Specification
specifications.relevance: Schema and execution semantics for GraphQL APIs.

specifications.name: gRPC Documentation
specifications.relevance: RPC design and operational guidance for gRPC services.

specifications.name: Protocol Buffers Documentation
specifications.relevance: Schema definition and compatibility rules for protobuf messages.

specifications.name: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
specifications.relevance: Current standard problem-details envelope for HTTP APIs; obsoletes RFC 7807.

tools.name: Spectral
tools.relevance: Artifact linting and style governance for OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and Arazzo documents.

tools.name: Prism
tools.relevance: Schema-aware mock server and request/response validator for OpenAPI and Postman collections.

tools.name: oasdiff
tools.relevance: OpenAPI diff and breaking-change detection for PR gates.

tools.name: Pact Documentation
tools.relevance: Consumer-driven contract testing, verification, and broker workflows.

tools.name: Pact Broker `can-i-deploy`
tools.relevance: Primary deployment-safety gate for Pact-based compatibility management.

tools.name: PactFlow
tools.relevance: Hosted Pact platform with broker, bi-directional workflows, and optional AI features.

tools.name: PactFlow Bi-Directional Contract Testing
tools.relevance: Primary reference for BDCT: how consumer contracts are cross-verified against provider OpenAPI specs server-side, when BDCT fits over classic CDC, and its tradeoffs. PactFlow-exclusive feature; not in open-source Pact Broker.

tools.name: PactFlow Agent Skills (formerly PactFlow MCP Server, Oct 2025)
tools.relevance: AI-powered contract/Drift test generation and maintenance inside IDEs, bundling the renamed SmartBear MCP Server (docs.pact.io/ai_tools/smartbear-mcp). Confirmed current as of docs page last-updated May 2026. Supports Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode, Codex, Kiro, Antigravity; available to PactFlow Cloud, on-premises, and Pact Broker users.

tools.name: PactFlow Drift
tools.relevance: Confirmed live as of mid-2026: spec-driven, OpenAPI-first API testing (CLI + CI-native) that validates whether a provider implementation matches its published spec, with AI-generated test scaffolding from the spec. Complements CDC/BDCT by answering 'does the provider spec reflect reality?' rather than 'are consumers compatible?'.

tools.name: Specmatic
tools.relevance: Executable contracts, backward-compatibility checks, and mixed protocol support. Specmatic 2.0 added GraphQL and gRPC support; Arazzo and Avro reached GA around Q3 2025. MCP (Model Context Protocol) testing support and WSDL are listed as shipped on the current roadmap page, but sources disagreed on exact GA timing — treat MCP/WSDL protocol-support claims as unverified as of 2026-07-11 and confirm against docs.specmatic.io/supported_protocols before citing specifics.

tools.name: Schemathesis
tools.relevance: Property-based test generation and schema validation for OpenAPI and GraphQL (GraphQL support confirmed still present as of the July 2, 2026 release). v4.0.0 released June 10, 2025 — full engine rewrite with breaking CLI changes: --hypothesis-max-examples renamed to --max-examples, --base-url renamed to --url, --show-trace and --validate-schema removed, schemathesis.io-related flags removed, new --phases/--report options, and a new schemathesis.toml config file.

tools.name: Schemathesis v3 to v4 Migration Guide
tools.relevance: Required reading before updating CI scripts from Schemathesis v3. Documents renamed flags, removed options (--app, --show-trace, schemathesis.io-related), and new --phases / --report options.

tools.name: Microcks
tools.relevance: Mocking and executable contract testing across REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and AsyncAPI. Accepted to CNCF Sandbox June 22, 2023; the CNCF TOC voted it to Incubating maturity on May 3, 2026 (645 contributors, 34 public adopters at time of promotion).

tools.name: Keploy
tools.relevance: Traffic-capture and replay workflow for bootstrapping regression tests on existing APIs.

tools.name: Buf
tools.relevance: Linting and breaking-change detection for protobuf and gRPC contracts.

tools.name: GraphQL Inspector
tools.relevance: Schema diffing and local GraphQL breaking-change checks.

tools.name: GraphQL Hive Schema Registry
tools.relevance: Schema registry and conditional GraphQL breaking-change checks using collected operations.

tools.name: Apollo GraphOS Schema Checks
tools.relevance: GraphQL build, operations, lint, and downstream contract checks.

tools.name: Postman Documentation
tools.relevance: Functional testing, governance, and AI-assisted exploration; best used as an adjunct rather than the primary contract authority. Postbot was relaunched as "Postman AI" / "Agent Mode" in the March 2026 platform update, gaining the ability to act on collections/tests/mocks and generate contract/load/unit/e2e tests directly — verify current agentic scope before granting write access.

tools.name: Dredd (ARCHIVED — do not use for new work)
tools.relevance: Dredd (apiaryio) was archived by the owner on November 8, 2024 — repository is read-only and no longer maintained. Apiary hosted product shut down September 2025 (unverified exact date as of 2026-07-11 — confirm before citing). Replace with Schemathesis, Specmatic, or Prism for provider-spec verification in BDCT workflows.

security.name: OWASP API Security
security.relevance: Security risk model for API security baselines, including authorization, resource consumption, and unsafe API consumption.
